report:
The retained restricted argument is mathematically correct. This verdict covers the divisorial limit proposition, the ordinary P-envelope argument, the specified transcendental product example, the dense-pole obstruction, and the mathematical content of n1–n4. It does not close original P15.3 or validate unrelated prior solver verdicts.

The four primary versions match the stated headers: DRWNXZ v3, 5 January 2026; Xia v2, 13 April 2024; Cao v1, 21 October 2012; and CHPW v5, 5 February 2018, with internal manuscript date 24 September 2018. The indispensable external results are listed below. Their applications respect the distinctions between class volume, actual nonpluripolar mass, multiplier-ideal volume, and Cao products.

For the restricted proposition, β+εΩ is smooth Kähler and Rε=[D]+β+εΩ is a gentle analytic Kähler current. Rationality of a is essential for the stated DRWNXZ admissibility. Adding D to a gentle residual current preserves gentleness: a common rational coefficient makes the exponential a product of smooth integer powers, and a common modification gives a divisorial potential with smooth remainder. Conversely, G⪯Rε forces ν(G,F)≥a. Divisor subtraction preserves positivity and analytic singularities. Applying subtraction to G−δΩ proves that G−[D] remains Kähler. It need not remain gentle; the analytic-current realization in the big residual class supplies its valuation. Recursive Lelong-number additivity and linear restriction then prove both inclusions of (2.2). Thus the partial-body equality is justified independently of simply citing Example 5.3.

The resulting intersection is ν(D)+Δ([β]). Every positive-level residual body contains the origin, so the intersection is nonempty. It is compact and convex. Adding a smooth positive form preserves every valuation coordinate. Pointwise comparisons cΩ<Ω′<CΩ yield cofinal inclusions and perturbation independence. For positive forms ρj tending uniformly to zero, choose cjΩ≤ρj≤δjΩ with δj→0. The inner limiting body and the outer fixed-form bodies sandwich the intermediate bodies. Compactness and the nested-intersection subsequence argument prove Hausdorff convergence. These arguments establish precisely the stated positive perturbations and paths; they establish no independence for arbitrary nonpositive paths.

The ordinary P-envelope proof supplies a bound independent of the competitor’s singularity constant. For normalized v≤0 with v≤φ+Cv, subtraction produces a β-psh residual w=v−φ with its canonical extension across F. On a compact complement of F, normalization bounds w uniformly. In each divisor chart, w plus a local potential of β is psh. Fixed transverse boundary circles avoid F, giving a uniform boundary bound for every smaller transverse disc. The subharmonic maximum principle, including the identically −∞ case, gives the same bound throughout each disc. A finite cover yields w≤K globally. The logarithmic upper bound survives upper regularization at F, while φ−sup φ supplies the lower bound. Hence Pθ[φ]=φ+O(1). With θ fixed, boundedly equivalent inputs have identical competitor families. Changes of Hermitian metric preserve the asserted bounded P-type; they need not preserve the envelope as an identical function.

The product computations also have the claimed restricted scope. Off F, T is β; locality and absence of pluripolar mass give ⟨T^k⟩NP=β^k. The constant analytic sequence satisfies all Cao conditions: L¹ convergence, curvature lower bounds tending to zero, unchanged singularity order, and the multiplier-ideal inclusion for every δ>0 and integer m. After normalization φ≤0, that inclusion follows directly from integrability monotonicity. Its absolutely continuous current is β, so Cao’s cohomological products are [β^k]. For another positive representative of the same bounded type, subtraction leaves β+dd^c b with bounded b. The displayed Bedford–Taylor telescoping identity is valid and proves cohomology [β^k]. Its bounded products do not charge F and therefore give the actual nonpluripolar extension. This proves actual cohomological invariance, without asserting equality of representative measures or a general identification with Cao products.

The transcendental surface input exists. For each nonzero integral alternating form, being of type (1,1) is a proper real-analytic condition on linear complex structures on R⁴. Properness follows by choosing a complex structure that fails invariance of that form. Avoiding these countably many loci by Baire gives a torus with no nonzero integral (1,1)-classes. A constant compatible Hermitian form is Kähler, and its class lies outside the real span of divisor classes.

The cutoff-log construction genuinely yields a smooth Kähler residual on the blowup. The inner logarithm is semipositive, and its cutoff annulus has uniformly bounded negative curvature, controlled by sufficiently small rational a. In blowup coordinates, subtraction leaves π*κform+a dd^c log(1+|t|²). On E the first term is positive normally and the second tangentially, with complementary kernels. Strict positivity follows there and nearby; the annulus and the remaining complement are controlled as stated. Thus κa=π*κ−a[E] is Kähler, rather than merely nef. Restriction to a generic product slice, followed where necessary by π*, π_*, verifies transcendence of the original and modified classes. The flag (3.2) is globally smooth, connected, and complete.

The nonbig psh pullback argument is valid. Descending off the exceptional image gives locally bounded-above psh potentials, which extend across that image. Their pullbacks agree almost everywhere with the original potentials, hence agree as canonical representatives. Surjectivity of the modification gives order reflection, normalization preservation, and preservation of bounded singularity inequalities. The resulting order isomorphism commutes with the least psh upper bounds defining the ordinary envelopes. No bigness hypothesis is smuggled into this argument, and no independence of unrelated modifications is asserted.

Both inclusions of (3.5) hold. For the upper inclusion, subtract the first valuation t[Y1]. Restriction to a generic curve fiber has degree ε−t and is positive, forcing 0≤t≤ε. Restriction to Y1 exists because the residual analytic potential is not identically −∞ there. Its class is κa+ε[η], since the normal bundle of the product fiber is trivial. Its remaining valuation lies in the big surface body. For the lower inclusion, the displayed product current is Kähler for rational 0≤t<ε and has valuation (t,ν(R)). Common rational coefficients ensure gentle singularities. Neither ε nor the transcendental surface class needs to be rational. Density of these t and of gentle surface valuations, followed by closure, includes the endpoint t=ε.

Continuity from above applies to the Kähler surface class κa. Consequently the limiting residual body is {0}×Δ(E,q)(κa), and ν(D)=(0,a,0) gives (3.3). The surface body contains the origin and has interior, so the intrinsic dimension is exactly two. Bounded truncation masses and Stokes bound the Kähler surface volume by its self-intersection, while a smooth representative attains it. The surface volume theorem and π*κ·E=0, E²=−1 therefore give 2 Area(B)=κ²−a²>0. The carrier and coordinate area are explicitly fixed. The degree-one transverse scale gives the same number by pairing β² with Ω0; changing that degree to m multiplies the pairing by m. The minimum second coordinate is a, establishing coefficient sensitivity for distinct rational a in the same original class.

Class volume zero is established independently: pairing a hypothetical Kähler current in α with θ² contradicts θ³=0 and ∫Ω∧θ²>0. Actual top mass is zero because β³=0, whereas [β²] is nonzero. The Cao current products have the same largest nonzero degree, two. The usual nef numerical dimension of α is also two. These are direct computations under this flag and reference scale, not consequences of Xia’s conjecture or CHPW’s projective theorem.

The dense-pole obstruction is complete. The coefficients sum to 1/4, the chordal logarithms have a uniform L¹ norm, and the decreasing series is a nontrivial θ-psh potential. Distributional convergence gives the stated positive current. Its bounded truncations are pulled back from P¹, so their surface top wedges vanish. The envelope is nontrivial because u is a competitor. For each j, competitor inclusion and the proved single-divisor envelope bound imply ψ≤aj gj+Kj, including after regularization. Thus every fiber pole survives. Any v≤ψ+C is −∞ on their dense union. Analytic singularities on any open neighborhood would give a closed holomorphic zero set containing a dense subset, forcing all generators to vanish identically and contradicting local integrability. The argument is independent of the background form and therefore applies to every positive Kähler perturbation and every flag center. It defeats exactly the specified analytic-domination recipe. Moreover, the envelope’s actual top mass is also zero: its bounded θ-psh truncations have total Bedford–Taylor mass ∫θ²=0.

The source limitations in n1 are correct. Xia’s construction retains I-equivalence, and its volume formula uses the actual mass of the I-envelope. His zero-volume dimension equality is explicitly conjectural. Cao’s current product is available here, while his line-bundle numerical definition and projective hypersurface reductions are not transcendental arbitrary-flag theorems. CHPW requires a positive volume subvariety in the flag; it is not applied to this example. Notes n2 and n3 faithfully summarize the checked proofs. Note n4 maintains the correct partial status and unresolved obligations. Its hashes, build logs, and execution assertions are documentary claims, not mathematical premises or evidence of correctness in this audit.

Two harmless wording corrections are needed: the residual Hausdorff limit becomes (2.1) after translation by ν(D), and Xia’s Chebyshev question concerns an auxiliary more-singular Kähler-current potential η, not an auxiliary positive form. Neither changes a proof. Arbitrary nonanalytic P-data, general numerical-dimension/flag results, and general modification independence remain open as stated.

passages.statement: DRWNXZ arXiv:2309.07584v3, Lemma 3.1, Definition 3.2, Propositions 3.3–3.4 and Theorem 7.6/Corollary 7.7: on a connected compact Kähler n-fold with a globally smooth connected complete flag, a big class’s body is closure ν(Ω(ξ))=closure ν(A(ξ,q)), compact convex with interior, and Δ(ξ)=∩ε>0Δ(ξ+ε[ω]). The intersection defines the pseudoeffective body independently of Kähler ω. In both cases vol_Rn Δ(ξ)=vol(ξ)/n!.

DRWNXZ v3, Lemma 2.5: a positive current T with ν(T,F)≥a∈Q≥0 along a prime divisor F has positive T−a[F], preserving local analytic singularities.

DRWNXZ v3, Definitions 2.6 and 5.1: gentleness requires c∈Q>0, the coherent-ideal model φ=c logΣ|f_i|²+O(1), smooth e^(φ/c), and divisorial pullback with smooth remainder on a Kähler modification. For big ξ and gentle analytic Kähler reference R, Δ(ξ;R)=closure ν{G∈Ω(ξ):G⪯R}.
Locally bounded-above psh functions extend across analytic subsets by upper regularization; canonical psh representatives agreeing almost everywhere coincide everywhere (DRWNXZ v3, Lemma 2.1 proof).

For locally bounded psh potentials, Bedford–Taylor products are closed positive currents and satisfy plurifine locality. When truncation masses are locally bounded, nonpluripolar products are determined by their bounded truncations and put no mass on pluripolar sets; for small unbounded locus they are the trivial extensions of the Bedford–Taylor products on its complement (BEGZ, arXiv:0812.3674v2, §1.2).

passages.statement: For positive currents T_i=θ_i+dd^cφ_i on a compact Kähler manifold, Cao v1, Definitions 2–3, require analytic approximants converging in L¹, θ_i+dd^cφ_i,j≥−τ_jω with τ_j→0, φ_i,j+1≤φ_i,j+O(1), and, for every δ>0 and m∈N, eventual I(m(1+δ)φ_i,j)⊂I(mφ_i). Their absolutely continuous wedge integrals define approximation-independent cohomological products. Definition 4 defines numerical dimension for a pseudoeffective line-bundle metric with positive curvature as the largest nonzero product degree.

passages.statement: Xia arXiv:2112.04290v2 constructs multiplier-ideal partial bodies in the smooth projective line-bundle setting. Equal multiplier ideals at every positive real scale give identical bodies; this I-invariance persists in §5.6’s intersection over rational positive ample perturbations (equation (1.2), Proposition 5.8 and §5.6).

For a pseudoeffective line bundle with psh metric φ on a smooth irreducible projective n-fold, writing ϕ for its potential relative to θ=c1(L,h), Xia v2, Theorem 2.19 gives lim_k k^−n h⁰(X,L^k⊗I(kφ))=(1/n!)∫X⟨(θ+dd^cPθ[ϕ]_I)^n⟩. On a compact Kähler manifold, Proposition 2.10 identifies Cθ[ϕ] with ordinary Pθ[ϕ] when the input’s actual top mass is positive.

Xia v2 labels dim Δ(θ,ϕ)=nd(θ,ϕ) in the projective line-bundle limit setting as Conjecture 5.29. In §6.4’s positive I-envelope-mass setting, independence of the Chebyshev transform from the more-singular Kähler-current potential η is left open.

CHPW arXiv:1508.03922v5, Corollary 3.22: for a pseudoeffective real divisor D on a smooth projective n-fold and an admissible flag containing a positive volume subvariety V=Y_(n−κν(D)), the limiting body lies in {0}^(n−κν(D))×R_≥0^κν(D), has dimension κν(D), and has intrinsic volume vol⁺_(X|V)(D)/κν(D)!. Here V has dimension κν(D), is not contained in B_−(D), and has positive augmented restricted volume. Remark 3.24 allows strict dimension inequality for other flags.
